prerequisites: Ability to read and understand documentation written in English

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity to ensure, manage, audit and certify the quality of developments, processes, systems, services, applications and IT products.
Understand the different standards and models applicable to the management and quality assurance of IT products and the improvement of their production processes.
Evaluate the production processes of IT products and services and propose improvements to them.
Plan and execute product quality evaluation processes using various verification, validation, and testing techniques.

syllabus_topics: Evaluation of quality: Methodologies, techniques and tools for unit testing.
Evaluation of quality: Methodologies, techniques and tools for system and static testing. Verification and Validation.
Planning and Management of testing processes: Test Governance.
Quality and testing standards. Process models and their improvement. Research.
Preparation and execution of the evaluation. Design, implementation and automation of Unit, System and Static tests.
Planning, evaluation management and defect correction.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory Practices: individual and/or group work during laboratory practices, continuous monitoring of individual contribution, delivery of reports, and final presentation.
Theory Assignments: specific individual or group assignments for theory classes, participation in classes and other activities.
On-site Test: final knowledge test with questions and/or exercises on theory contents.

assessment_rules: To pass the course, each of the three blocks (Laboratory Practices, Theory Assignments, On-site Test) must be approved with a minimum score of 5 out of 10. The final grade is calculated as 0.6 x Lab Practices + 0.2 x Theory Assignments + 0.2 x On-site Test. If any block is not approved, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. Students with 80% attendance in theory classes may be exempt from the on-site test, with their final grade calculated as (0.6 x Lab Practices + 0.2 x Theory Assignments) x 10/8. For the extraordinary examination, if laboratory practices and theory assignments were approved in the ordinary examination, their scores are maintained; otherwise, they are 0. A new on-site theoretical and practical test is conducted, requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10 to pass. The final grade is calculated as 0.6 x On-site Test + 0.4 x Assignment Grade (where Assignment Grade = 0.25 x Theory Assignments + 0.75 x Lab Practices).
